clue.text: Gossip listened to in this place, for example

indicators.note: something listened to is heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: in this place means here, and for example means say, as in 'take, say, Paris'

explanation.surface: Someone passes on rumours they overheard at this spot, giving an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase HERE SAY, said out loud, sounds exactly like the word for rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is talk passed on second-hand, which is a synonym for gossip.

clue.text: Saves many people, so we've heard

indicators.note: a phrase about hearing tells the solver that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: hordes are large crowds of many people

explanation.surface: A rumour says someone rescues a great number of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saves' looks like rescuing; here it means stores up, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to store things away and keep them, a synonym for saving.

clue.text: Gladstone's adviser working in support of statute

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece in support of another sits beneath it

parts.note: a statute is an act of parliament
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A Victorian prime minister's adviser is busy backing a law.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Acton, the historian, was a close adviser and friend of the Liberal prime minister William Gladstone.
explanation.definitionFit: The historian Lord Acton was a confidant of Gladstone, so he is a fair example of an adviser to him.

clue.text: Inane pets running wild for many years

indicators.note: animals running wild are out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Silly pets have been running loose for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of INANE PETS gives the plural of a seven-year span.
explanation.definitionFit: A septennium is a seven-year period, so the plural stands for a long run of years.

clue.text: Sign of victory eludes Frenchman? That's right

indicators.note: a letter that eludes a word escapes it, so it is taken out

parts.note: Yves is a typical French man's name
V is the victory sign, made with two fingers

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fails to make the V-sign, and someone agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying yes affirms that a statement is correct, an everyday equivalent of agreeing it is so.

clue.text: Lead attack on union rate

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A leader directs an assault on the trade union's pay rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a verb but is the metal; 'rate' reads as a pay level but is the old verb meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone, in an older sense, is to scold them angrily, a synonym of reproaching.

clue.text: Blind drunk, bosun goes to tavern, staggering

indicators.note: staggering about suggests letters lurching out of their order
a drunk sailor is muddled, signalling that his letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A ship's officer, very drunk, heads unsteadily for the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind drunk' reads as one phrase; 'Blind' alone is the definition, the drunk bosun is scrambled, then mixed again with the tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: To be blind to things is to fail to notice them, so it means lacking in observation.

clue.text: Timber — a large chunk? The reverse

indicators.note: the clue tells the solver to take the phrase the opposite way round

parts.note: a slab is a large thick piece

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a piece of wood is a big lump, then says it is the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: A SLAB read backwards gives the light wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood used for models, a kind of timber.

clue.text: An arduous task, securing it for religious recluse

indicators.note: a word securing another holds it fast inside

parts.note: a chore is a tiresome task

explanation.surface: A hard job fixing something, done for a hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arduous task' sounds like hard labour for a monk, but it is only a household job holding the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a hermit who withdraws from the world for prayer.

clue.text: Making provisional plans for conscription?

definitions.meaning: writing a rough first version of a plan
the draft is the American term for compulsory call-up into the forces

explanation.walkthrough: The word is both the act of writing a rough version and, as a noun, the call-up into military service.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version, and also the call-up of recruits, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Italian food required? For the present, presumably, nothing's provided

parts.note: someone for the present is against the past, written as anti plus past
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether an Italian dish is wanted now, since nothing has been supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful reading: being in favour of the present means being against the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course of cold meats and vegetables, a type of Italian food.

clue.text: Fabric used in lovely craftwork

indicators.note: the letters needed are contained within the following words of the clue

explanation.surface: A stretchy material appears in a fine piece of handicraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a stretch synthetic material, a brand of fabric.

clue.text: First of tomes penned by Scandinavian writer

indicators.note: something penned by another is shut inside it, as in a pen

parts.note: a Dane is a person from Denmark, in Scandinavia

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian author writes the opening volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy, is a famous Italian writer.

clue.text: Search those in a scene at a boxing match

parts.note: the cast are the actors appearing in a scene
a bout is a single contest in boxing

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for the actors in a scene shot at a prize fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast about is to look around in all directions, an idiom for searching.

clue.text: State-of-the-art razor?

definitions.meaning: describing the most advanced, newest position in a field
a razor is literally a tool with a sharp blade for slicing

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: a razor is an edge that cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The most advanced stage of development is called its leading front, and a razor literally has a blade for slicing.

clue.text: Back in business, people worry

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the first word is placed inside the letters of the combined pair

parts.note: a nation is a people
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Back at work, the staff are anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as returning to work but is the rear of a ship, set into the company and people pair after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is anxious dismay, which is a kind of worry.

clue.text: Stone-worker-see-having heart cut out in horror film

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the film's name

parts.note: a chiller is a frightening film

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the word see is taken as written before its centre goes

explanation.surface: A mason sees his heart removed in a scary movie.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE loses its middle E to give SE, which goes into CHILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who carves stone with a chisel is a stone-worker; the word also means a swindler.

clue.text: Beastly worshipper disconcerted saint going round part of Africa

indicators.note: the scrambled letters surround the country's name
a disconcerted person is thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An upset saint touring Africa meets a worshipper of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted' rearranges the saint into ANIST, whose first three letters sit before the African country and the last two after.
explanation.definitionFit: An animalist worships animals, so a beastly worshipper is a humorous phrase for one.

clue.text: In that French exam, one's least likely to speak

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: que is French for that
one is the Roman numeral I
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: During a French exam, someone is the most reluctant to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The most silent person is the one with the least to say, a paraphrase of least likely to speak.

clue.text: Dull university publication, one read by local inhabitant

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication
one is the Roman numeral I
a native is someone born in a place

explanation.surface: A boring college magazine is read by one local person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking imagination makes a person or thing dull, a close synonym.

clue.text: Group trailed by Italian outlaw

indicators.note: a word trailed by another has it coming behind

parts.note: a band is a group

explanation.surface: A gang is followed by an Italian criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, an outlaw.

clue.text: Order Tories to appear on E4

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece appearing on another follows it

parts.note: the letter E followed by the solution to clue 4, a cross-reference
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians are told to go on the E4 television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: E4 is a British TV channel, but here 4 refers to the answer of 4 down, put after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes right is a drill command telling soldiers to turn their heads, a military order.

clue.text: Rinse out sticky substance

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Wash away something gummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky sap from trees, a gummy substance.

clue.text: First character to give expression of surprise about old record

indicators.note: one word goes around another

parts.note: aha is what someone says on a discovery
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

explanation.surface: Someone gives a gasp of surprise at a vintage record.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the opening letter of the Greek alphabet, its first character.

clue.text: Cheapest offers include sauce

indicators.note: the words include the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: The lowest priced deals come with a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Measure applied to island, one near New York

indicators.note: applied to means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A measurement is used on an island close to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellis Island, in New York Harbour, was the immigrant entry station.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Island sits in the harbour beside New York City, so it is one near the city.

clue.text: Put out, girl's failed to meet target

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, with the possessive
to have missed is to fail to hit the target

explanation.surface: A girl is out because she missed her target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' sounds like upset; it means sent away, as a batter is out in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dismissed is to be sent away or out, as from a job or in cricket.

clue.text: Out of spirits? Oddly, shandy will do

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters, first, third and fifth, are taken

explanation.surface: Someone down in the dumps is told a shandy will cheer them.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a mild drink, which plays on 'spirits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low in mood is being out of spirits, so a synonym for unhappy.

clue.text: Recent translation by English dramatist

indicators.note: a translation changes words into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new rendering of an English playwright's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman comic playwright, so he is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: City editor changed tabloid heading

indicators.note: changed means the letters are reordered
the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A city newspaper editor alters a tabloid's headline.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a city in Michigan, home of the US car industry.
